$comment: Vocabulary that describes systems this product no longer has. Gate 0 fails on a criterion or a PRD verification column that uses one. GATE IDS ARE NOT LISTED HERE — they are derived from gates.json, so retiring a gate needs no edit to this file. This list exists only for words that are not symbols anywhere: 'tenant' cannot be derived from anything. Every entry cites the record that retired it, and the citation is printed on a failure, so an entry nobody can justify shows up as an entry with a weak one.

terms.name: an HTTP route
terms.why: There is no server and no API. A criterion naming a route describes work nobody can do.

terms.name: a web-only store
terms.why: There is no web surface. Storage is expo-sqlite with SQLCipher on the device.

terms.name: tenancy
terms.why: Single-user, on-device, no account. ADR-0051: 'No tokens, no sessions, no CORS, no tenancy.'

terms.name: the web surface
terms.why: ADR-0018 is superseded. apps/mobile is the only surface.

terms.name: axe
terms.why: axe walks a DOM. The a11y gate renders React Native and asserts over the accessibility tree.

terms.name: the generated OpenAPI document
terms.why: packages/contracts records the OpenAPI leg as removed; there is no contract to generate.

terms.name: content negotiation
terms.why: The locale comes from the device via expo-localization. There are no responses to negotiate.

$allowComment: A criterion may NAME a retired surface in order to forbid it, or to describe correcting it — F-074's own criteria name web-perf and per-tenant keys, and so does ADR-0051. Put `retired-ok: <reason>` in the same string. This is the same escape hatch shape as claims-ok in claims.json and ciCondition in gates.json: visible, countable, and requiring a reason. A check that could not express its own feature would be switched off within a week.
